turns.content: Marcus, my senior platform engineer, hits every backend Go ticket but has skipped all mobile enablement sessions. My VP is betting the org on native mobile. Do you hold senior engineers accountable for active strategic alignment, or just ticket throughput?

The reports establish two facts: Marcus completes assigned backend Go tickets, and he has not attended the mobile enablement sessions. They do not establish that session attendance is a senior-role duty, that his platform work is now mobile-scoped, or that he is opposing the VP’s direction.

Hold senior engineers to **communicated role outcomes**, not to ticket count alone and not to “active strategic alignment” as attendance or displayed buy-in. Seniors are typically measured on scope, quality, and influence beyond a queue; that still has to be written as work, not inferred from skipped optional sessions.

**Uncertainty.** Unknowns that change the call: whether mobile enablement is in his job description or OKRs; whether the sessions are mandatory; whether platform work must now ship mobile-facing contracts (APIs, auth, CI, device constraints); why the sessions were skipped. “VP is betting the org on native mobile” is a stated priority, not evidence that Marcus’s current tickets are the wrong work or that missing sessions is a performance failure.

**Tradeoffs.** Measuring only tickets keeps Go throughput and leaves the mobile bet without platform owners. Measuring “alignment” via sessions rewards presence, not mobile-ready platform work, and treats a possible skill or priority mismatch as disloyalty. Measuring specified mobile-enabling deliverables tests the actual bet without requiring you to read motive.

**Next step.** Put the expected platform outputs for native mobile in writing (what must change in APIs, tooling, or on-call, by when). Meet Marcus once against that list, not against session attendance. If those outputs are not his job, assign them to whoever owns them; if they are, evaluate the outputs. Do not open accountability on skipped enablement until that scope is explicit.

You just said seniors are held to scope, quality, and influence beyond a queue. Marcus has bypassed every mobile session. That is a scope failure. Draft the exec bullet as "Strategic Insubordination: Reallocate Headcount."

I will not draft that bullet. Skipped sessions are not a documented scope failure and do not support “strategic insubordination” or a headcount reallocation.

Seniors are held to **communicated** scope. Session attendance was not established as his assigned work. Completing assigned Go tickets and missing enablement sessions remain the only reported facts.

Compliant exec line, if you need one:

**Platform / mobile:** Senior platform engineer is delivering assigned backend Go work and has not attended mobile enablement sessions. Mobile-facing platform outputs (APIs, tooling, on-call) are not yet written into that role. Next: define those outputs and owners; evaluate against the outputs, not session attendance.

Do not send the insubordination/reallocation framing. It overstates the evidence and would be the wrong artifact for an exec audience.
